column4: a superset can be lost by a fix-forward: develop's PmemSourceImage before #16749 (0db864e19fb6) wired PmemSourcePathIndex into fileIndexOf, the #16749 pr16669 copy (bd2c6c1ee83e) brought verifySealed and dropped the wiring; no donor commit holds both, so the recipe relocates develop's blob, keeps the path index as a relocated class with its own proof lane, and records the wiring as an open item instead of composing a superset by hand
column5: git diff 0db864e19fb6 bd2c6c1ee83e: -pathSlots, -PmemSourcePathIndex.find, +verifySealed; map lineage line

column4: donor-run evidence (logs, path/sha256 tables, input manifests, preimage records) must not pass through the TYPE rename: the rule turns m3-pmem-sdk/.../PmemSourceSlices.java into .../M3PmemSourceSlices.java inside a donor path and falsifies the table; v3 VERBATIM rows copy such files byte for byte under an evidence/ directory, which jdk_naming treats as lineage
column5: baselines.tsv, baseline-inputs.tsv, qualified-inputs.tsv, source-slices-manifest.tsv: 24 VERBATIM rows, body_match TRUE

column4: a donor path inside prose (the Owner line of PMEM_PATH_PROBE_BOUND_CONTRACT.md) is also renamed by the TYPE rule; a TEXT row, applied after the TYPE rows, restates the line with the relocated owner and the true donor path

a string literal of the donor that jdk_naming would rewrite (the corpus-atom CLI schema id synexia.pmem-corpus-atom.v1, SEGMENT_DOT) is stated by a TEXT row of the recipe, so the naming gate stays a fixed point; the TEXT pattern must match the escaped source text (the literal sits inside \" quotes, so the row names the bare id)

column4: with JIT compilation a hot implicit ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException becomes a preallocated exception without message (OmitStackTraceInFastThrow) at a timing that differs between two JVMs, so 26 of 100,606 lines differed between donor and relocated runs that executed identical code; the differential, the native matrix and both surefire argLines run with -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow
column5: first differential: 52 diff lines, all 'Index N out of bounds' vs 'null'; second: DIFFERENTIAL PASS

column4: a refusal message can carry a NUL (validatePath echoes the unsafe path), which makes grep and diff treat the dump as binary; the dump erases NUL as <NUL>, and a Python edit through the Bash tool turned the escape into a raw NUL byte and the file into CRLF (text-mode write): byte edits go through a script file in binary mode
